title: Hoh Rain Forest
description: One of the largest temperate rain forests in the United States, getting up to 14 feet of rain a year.
overview_points: Towering Sitka spruce, western hemlock, Douglas fir, and bigleaf maple covered in green moss
Fern-covered ground, clear streams, and dense canopies with soft light
Home to Roosevelt elk, black bears, banana slugs, and many birds, plants, and fungi
highlights: 🌲 Ancient trees over 300 feet tall
🍃 Moss-covered branches with a storybook feel
🥾 Easy walking trails like the Hall of Mosses and Spruce Nature Trail
🦌 Frequent Roosevelt elk sightings
🌧 Lush greenery all year long

best_time.heading: Beautiful in Every Season
seasons: Spring: Wildflowers bloom, rivers run high
Summer: Mild and driest — best for hiking
Fall: Colorful leaves, fewer visitors
Winter: Mist and moss give a magical feel

tips: Wear waterproof shoes and bring a rain jacket, even in summer
Arrive early — parking fills fast in peak season
Stay on designated trails to protect the ecosystem
Keep distance from wildlife and follow Leave No Trace

title: Hurricane Hill Trail
description: An iconic paved trail with big views for little effort, climbing gently through alpine meadows to the summit of Hurricane Hill.
overview_points: Sweeping views of the Olympic Mountains, Strait of Juan de Fuca, and Vancouver Island
Summer wildflowers and wildlife like Olympic marmots and black-tailed deer
Great spot for sunrise, sunset, and stargazing
highlights: 🏔 Spectacular 360-degree mountain and coastal views
🌸 Seasonal wildflowers in alpine meadows
🦌 Frequent wildlife sightings
🚶 Smooth, paved trail for a wide range of hikers
📸 One of the park's most photographed viewpoints

best_time.heading: Late Spring – Early Fall
seasons: July–September has the clearest weather and best wildflowers
Early mornings are cooler, quieter, and have softer light

tips: Dress in layers — temperatures and winds change fast up high
Bring water, sun protection, and a camera
Stay on designated trails to protect alpine plants
Check road and trail conditions before visiting

title: Franklin Falls
description: A popular, family-friendly waterfall hike near Snoqualmie Pass ending at a 70-foot cascade.
overview_points: Trail follows the South Fork Snoqualmie River through cedar and fir forest
Mist and rushing water create a refreshing atmosphere at the base
Great for families, beginners, and quick adventures
highlights: 💧 Stunning 70-foot waterfall over rugged cliffs
🌲 Scenic forest trail with moss and river views
🥾 Short, beginner-friendly hike for all ages
📸 Great photography all year
❄️ Frozen waterfall views in winter

best_time.heading: Great Year-Round
seasons: Spring: Powerful water flow from snowmelt
Summer: Warm and easy — ideal for families
Fall: Golden foliage backdrop
Winter: Frozen falls — traction devices may be needed

tips: Wear sturdy footwear — trail can be muddy or slippery
Go early or on weekdays to avoid crowds
View the falls from safe, designated spots
Pack out trash and follow Leave No Trace

title: Rattlesnake Ledge
description: One of Washington's most iconic day hikes, just a short drive from Seattle, climbing through forest to a dramatic rocky ledge.
overview_points: Views of Rattlesnake Lake and the Cascade foothills
Well-maintained path through Douglas firs and hemlocks
Suitable for hikers of all experience levels
highlights: 🏞 Panoramic overlook of Rattlesnake Lake
🌲 Towering evergreens and seasonal wildflowers
🥾 Well-maintained path for beginners and experienced hikers
📸 One of the most photographed viewpoints near Seattle
🌅 Beautiful sunrise and sunset views

best_time.heading: Accessible Year-Round
seasons: Spring/summer: green and warm
Fall: colorful foliage
Winter: peaceful but possibly icy

tips: Arrive early or go on weekdays to avoid crowds
Wear sturdy shoes and bring plenty of water
Stay behind safety barriers — avoid unstable cliff edges
Keep pets leashed and follow Leave No Trace
Check weather and trail conditions, especially in winter

title: Skyline Loop Trail
description: A premier loop hike starting at the Paradise area, climbing through subalpine landscapes with views of Mount Rainier.
overview_points: Wildflower meadows, waterfalls, and glacier views
Marmots, mountain goats, and many birds along the way
One of the most photographed trails in the Pacific Northwest
highlights: 🏔 Close-up views of Mount Rainier and its glaciers
🌸 Alpine meadows full of seasonal wildflowers
💧 Scenic stops like Myrtle Falls and mountain streams
🦌 Marmots, mountain goats, and native wildlife
📸 Panoramic viewpoints over valleys and peaks

best_time.heading: Mid-July – September
seasons: Snow-free with peak wildflowers and best weather
Early mornings: cooler, fewer crowds, best photos

tips: Sturdy shoes and layers — mountain weather changes fast
Bring water, snacks, and sun protection (lots of exposure)
Stay on designated paths to protect the alpine ecosystem
Check trail and weather conditions — snow can linger into summer

title: Fremont Lookout
description: A classic alpine hike from the Sunrise area to a historic fire lookout high above the landscape.
overview_points: Ridgelines and open meadows with constant Mount Rainier views
Summer wildflowers, mountain goats, marmots, and birds of prey
Restored lookout with 360-degree views of the Cascades
highlights: 🏔 Uninterrupted views of Mount Rainier and glaciers
🛖 Historic fire lookout with panoramic scenery
🌸 Alpine meadows and seasonal wildflowers
🦌 Frequent marmot and mountain goat sightings
📸 Exceptional sunrise and sunset photography

best_time.heading: July – Early October
seasons: Snow melted and alpine flowers in bloom
Late afternoon/evening hikes are popular for golden light and sunsets

tips: Bring warm layers — cool temps and strong winds even in summer
Carry water, snacks, and sun protection (exposed trail)
Stay on designated paths to protect alpine plants
Check conditions — mountain weather changes fast

title: Maple Pass Loop
description: One of Washington's most celebrated alpine hikes, climbing through forest to open ridgelines with views in every direction.
overview_points: Crystal-clear lakes, rugged peaks, and colorful meadows
Famous for golden larches and fall colors
Summer wildflowers, marmots, and mountain goats
highlights: 🏔 Panoramic views of the North Cascades
🍂 Stunning golden larches and fall foliage
💧 Overlooks of Lake Ann and alpine tarns
🌸 Colorful wildflower meadows in summer
📸 Premier landscape photography destination

best_time.heading: Late June – October
seasons: Summer: lush meadows and clear views
Late September – early October: famous golden larch season

tips: Hike clockwise for a more gradual climb and steady views
Bring layers — weather changes fast even in summer
Carry water, snacks, and sun protection for exposed sections
Stay on marked trails and follow Leave No Trace

title: Colchuck Lake Trail
description: An alpine adventure leading to one of Washington's most stunning glacial lakes, at the edge of the Enchantments.
overview_points: Pine forests and granite landscapes leading to turquoise water
Framed by the towering peaks of the Stuart Range
Popular with day hikers and photographers
highlights: 💎 Vibrant turquoise glacial lake with granite peaks
🏔 Views of Dragontail Peak and the Stuart Range
🌲 Forest trails with streams and wildflowers
📸 Excellent reflection photography
🥾 Gateway to the famous Enchantments wilderness

best_time.heading: Late June – October
seasons: Summer: warm hiking and wildflowers
Early fall: crisp air, golden larches, colorful scenery

tips: Start early — parking fills quickly in peak season
Sturdy shoes for rocky, uneven terrain
Bring water, snacks, and layers
Follow Leave No Trace in the fragile alpine area
Check trail conditions and required permits before going

title: Mount Si Trail
description: An iconic, challenging climb near North Bend, popular as a training hike with rewarding summit views.
overview_points: Switchbacks through evergreen forest up to rocky terrain
Views of the Snoqualmie Valley and Cascade peaks
Optional scramble to the Haystack near the summit
highlights: 🏔 Panoramic views of the Snoqualmie Valley and Cascades
🌲 Forest trail lined with Douglas firs and cedars
🪨 Optional Haystack scramble for adventurous hikers
🌿 Seasonal wildflowers and abundant wildlife
📸 One of the most popular hikes near Seattle

best_time.heading: Accessible Year-Round
seasons: Spring/summer: lush and warm
Fall: vibrant foliage and crisp air
Winter: snowy scenery — needs proper gear and experience

tips: Start early for parking, especially on weekends
Sturdy shoes and plenty of water for the sustained climb
Dress in layers — temps vary between trailhead and summit
Use caution around exposed rock sections
Follow Leave No Trace on this heavily visited trail

title: High Divide and Seven Lakes Basin Loop
description: One of the most spectacular backcountry routes in Olympic National Park, mixing mountain ridgelines with alpine lakes.
overview_points: Climbs from rainforest to high alpine terrain
Views of the Olympic Mountains, including Mount Olympus on clear days
Popular multi-day backpacking trip; sometimes done as a long day hike
highlights: 🏔 Ridge views of the Olympics and Mount Olympus
💧 Seven alpine lakes in glacial basins
🌲 Transition from rainforest to alpine ecosystems
🦌 Black bears, marmots, and deer in remote habitat
📸 Exceptional backpacking scenery

best_time.heading: Mid-July – September
seasons: Summer: best for hiking and camping, wildflowers, long daylight
Early fall: cooler temps and fewer crowds
Snow can linger into early summer up high

tips: Wilderness permit required for overnight backpacking
Expect big elevation gain and changing mountain weather
Carry bear-proof food storage; follow Leave No Trace strictly
Bring layers for rainforest humidity and alpine wind
Reserve campsites in advance during peak season

title: Marmot Pass Trail
description: A classic Olympic Peninsula hike in the Buckhorn Wilderness, climbing from forest to a high alpine saddle.
overview_points: Old-growth forest, open meadows, and rocky ridgelines
Views of Buckhorn Mountain, Copper Peak, and the Strait of Juan de Fuca on clear days
Named for the playful marmots often seen near the pass
highlights: 🏔 Expansive alpine views of the Olympic Mountains
🌲 Transition from old-growth forest to subalpine meadows
🌸 Summer wildflowers near the pass
🦫 Frequent marmot sightings in rocky zones
📸 Excellent ridge photography spots

best_time.heading: July – Early October
seasons: Summer: most reliable conditions and full wildflower bloom
Early fall: cooler air, fewer hikers

tips: Long, moderately strenuous hike with steady elevation gain
Bring layers — warm forest to windy alpine ridges
Carry plenty of water and navigation tools
Don't feed or approach marmots and goats
Snow can linger at higher elevations into summer

title: Gothic Basin Trail
description: A rugged, dramatic alpine hike near Granite Falls, climbing steeply into a glacier-carved basin.
overview_points: Jagged peaks and granite walls around small reflective tarns
Beneath the towering Sloan Peak
Final section often requires scrambling over boulders and loose rock
highlights: 🏔 Dramatic alpine basin with jagged peaks and cliffs
💧 Beautiful tarns reflecting Sloan Peak
🌲 Steep forest climb into high alpine terrain
🌸 Seasonal wildflowers among rocks and snowfields
📸 One of the most striking alpine spots near Seattle

best_time.heading: Late July – September
seasons: Snow mostly melted from the basin
Early summer may still have snow crossings; fall is cooler and quieter

tips: Strenuous hike with big elevation gain and rocky scrambling
Sturdy boots with good traction for unstable terrain
Extra layers — the basin can be cold and windy even in summer
Carry navigation tools and check conditions first
Follow Leave No Trace — fragile alpine environment

title: Carne Mountain
description: A striking alpine hike in the eastern North Cascades near the Entiat River Valley with long ridgeline views.
overview_points: Forested slopes giving way to subalpine wildflowers and rocky outcrops
Views of Glacier Peak and the rugged Entiat Mountains
Broad, exposed ridge feels remote — no technical climbing required
highlights: 🏔 Wide-open ridge views of Glacier Peak and the Cascades
🌸 Vibrant subalpine wildflowers mid–late summer
🌲 Scenic transition from forest to open alpine terrain
📸 Panoramic viewpoints with minimal crowds
🐾 Mountain goats and other alpine wildlife

best_time.heading: July – September
seasons: Snow melted from the ridge, wildflowers in bloom
Early season: lingering snow patches; fall: crisp air, quieter trails

tips: Long, strenuous hike — start early and pace yourself
Bring layers for the windy, exposed ridge
Plenty of water and sun protection (limited shade up high)
Check trail conditions after snowmelt or storms
Stay on established paths to protect alpine plants

title: Ptarmigan Ridge Trail
description: One of Washington's most spectacular high-alpine hikes, in the Mount Baker Wilderness.
overview_points: Exposed ridgelines and alpine meadows starting near Artist Point
Mount Baker and the Coleman Glacier dominate the views
On clear days, see deep into the North Cascades and across to the Olympics
highlights: 🏔 Constant views of Mount Baker and the Coleman Glacier
🌄 Expansive alpine ridgelines with dramatic drop-offs
🌸 Seasonal wildflowers across high meadows
❄️ Lingering snowfields well into summer
📸 One of the most photogenic ridge hikes in Washington

best_time.heading: July – September
seasons: Early season may still have significant snow
Late summer: best balance of clear trails and vibrant scenery

tips: Be ready for snow travel early season (traction devices, trekking poles)
Warm layers and wind protection — constant exposure on the ridge
Carry navigation tools — snow can hide parts of the trail
Start early to avoid afternoon weather changes
Follow Leave No Trace in fragile alpine areas
